   100	  syntax Bool ::= isKwV(Val) [function, total]
   101	  rule isKwV(kwV(_:String, _:Val)) => true
   102	  rule isKwV(_:Val)                => false [owise]
   103	
   104	  // the frame marker carries the CONCRETE cellvar list, so cell-write dispatch
   105	  // decides by pnMember even over an abstract frame rest (no prover branching)
   106	  syntax Val ::= cellsMark(ParamNames)
   107	  syntax ParamNames ::= cellsOf(Val) [function]
   108	  rule cellsOf(cellsMark(CVS:ParamNames)) => CVS
   109	  syntax Bool ::= pnMember(String, ParamNames) [function, total]
   110	  rule pnMember(_:String, .ParamNames) => false
   111	  rule pnMember(X:String, (P:String, R:ParamNames)) => X ==String P orBool pnMember(X, R)
   112	
   113	  syntax KItem ::= #cellW(Val, Val)
   114	  rule <k> #cellW(cellRef(H:Int), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
   115	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(_:Val => V) ... </heap>
   116	
   117	  syntax KItem ::= #alloc(Val)
   118	  rule <k> #alloc(V:Val) => ref(N) ... </k>
   119	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> V) H </heap>
   120	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
   121	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
   122	
   123	  // ==== module load + statement sequencing ==================================
   124	  syntax KItem ::= #loadAll(Module)
   125	  rule <k> #loadAll(Module(SS:Stmts)) => SS ... </k>
   126	  rule <k> (S:Stmt SS:Stmts):Stmts => S ~> SS ... </k>
   127	  rule <k> .Stmts => .K ... </k>
   128	
   129	  // ==== Name lookup (walk the scope chain; builtins live in the -1 scope) ====
   130	  syntax KItem ::= #look(String, Int)
   131	  rule <k> Name(X:String) => #look(X, L) ... </k> <env> L:Int </env>
   132	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => {M[X]}:>Val ... </k>
   133	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   134	       requires X in_keys(M)
   135	  // a SYNTACTICALLY cell-bound name reads through the heap cell AT THE
   136	  // LOOKUP (higher priority beats the plain return above on concrete cell
   137	  // bindings; abstract claim values take the plain rule unchanged) — this
   138	  // covers cross-frame cell reads (a comprehension closure reading the
   139	  // enclosing function's cellvar) without a narrowing-prone k-top redex
   140	  // guarded on the FOUND frame's DECLARED cellvars (pnMember over the
   141	  // cellsMark): decidable for every concrete frame pin — plain frames and
   142	  // non-cell names prune outright, so an abstract looked-up value never
   143	  // drags a narrowing cellV heap match along (probed on 5-intersperse and
   144	  // Q4's abstract `numbers` in the annotated frame)
   145	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => V ... </k>
   146	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   147	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
   148	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool "$cells" in_keys(M)
   149	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
   150	        andBool {M[X]}:>Val ==K cellRef(H)
   151	       [priority(40)]
   152	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => #look(X, P) ... </k>
   153	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, parent(P:Int)) ... </scopes>
   154	       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
   155	
   156	  // the ONE predefined builtins scope (the -1 frame; claims write `-1 |-> builtinsScope`)
   157	  syntax Scope ::= "builtinsScope" [function, total]
   158	  rule builtinsScope
   159	    => scope(.Map [ "len"    <- builtinV("len")    ]
   160	                  [ "set"    <- builtinV("set")    ]
   161	                  [ "sum"    <- builtinV("sum")    ]
   162	                  [ "abs"    <- builtinV("abs")    ]
   163	                  [ "min"    <- builtinV("min")    ]
   164	                  [ "max"    <- builtinV("max")    ]
   165	                  [ "ord"    <- builtinV("ord")    ]
   166	                  [ "chr"    <- builtinV("chr")    ]
   167	                  [ "range"  <- builtinV("range")  ]
   168	                  [ "all"    <- builtinV("all")    ]
   169	                  [ "any"    <- builtinV("any")    ]
   170	                  [ "zip"    <- builtinV("zip")    ]
   171	                  [ "isinstance" <- builtinV("isinstance") ]
   172	                  [ "sorted" <- builtinV("sorted") ]
   173	                  [ "list"   <- builtinV("list")   ]
   174	                  [ "round"  <- builtinV("round")  ]
   175	                  [ "bin"    <- builtinV("bin")    ]
   176	                  [ "enumerate" <- builtinV("enumerate") ]
   177	                  [ "map"    <- builtinV("map")    ]
   178	                  [ "eval"   <- builtinV("eval")   ]
   179	                  [ "int"    <- typeV("int")       ]
   180	                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
   181	                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)
   182	
   183	  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
   184	  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
   185	  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
   186	  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   187	                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   188	                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
   189	  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
   190	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
   191	  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>
   192	
   193	  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
   194	  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
   195	  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
   196	  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>
   197	
   198	  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
   199	  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
   200	  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
   201	  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
   202	  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
   203	  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
   204	  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   205	  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   206	
   207	  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
   208	  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
   209	  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
   210	  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]
   211	
   212	  // ==== shared list helpers ======================…2064 tokens truncated… where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
    25	  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
    26	  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).
    27	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => Assign(Name(X), BinOp(OP, Name(X), V)) ... </k>
    28	       <env> L:Int </env>
    29	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    30	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
    34	  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
    35	  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
    37	  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
    38	  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    39	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    40	       <env> L:Int </env>
    41	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    42	       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
    43	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    44	       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")
    45	
    46	  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
    47	  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
    48	  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>
    49	
    50	  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
    51	  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
    52	  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
    54	  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>
    55	
    56	  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
    57	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
    58	       requires truthy(V)
    59	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
    60	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    61	
    62	  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
    63	  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
    64	  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
    65	  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
    66	                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
    67	                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"
    68	
    69	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, OBJ:Val, B:Stmts) => #loop(OBJ, T, B) ... </k>
    70	
    71	  rule <k> #loop(IT:Iterable, T:Expr, B:Stmts) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #loopStep(T, B) ... </k>
    72	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #loopStep(_:Expr, _:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    73	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, REST:Iterable) ~> #loopStep(T:Expr, B:Stmts)
    74	        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> B ~> #loopLbl(#loop(REST, T, B)) ... </k>
    75	
    76	  // ==== While ==============================================================
    77	  rule <k> While(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => #while(C, B) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #while(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => C ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
    79	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => B ~> #loopLbl(#while(C, B)) ... </k>
    80	       requires truthy(V)
    81	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(_C:Expr, _B:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    82	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    83	
    84	  // ==== loop control (break / continue) =====================================
    85	  rule <k> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    86	  rule <k> Continue => #cont ... </k>
    87	  rule <k> Break => #brk ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #cont ~> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #cont ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    90	  rule <k> #brk ~> #loopLbl(_:K) => .K ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #brk ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    92	
    93	  // ==== heap-object deref at the truthiness/iteration consumers ==============
    94	  // (priority(40) preempts the generic Val rules so truthy/#loop never see a ref)
    95	  rule <k> If(ref(H:Int), T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => If(V, T, E) ... </k>
    96	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    97	       [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> IfExp(ref(H:Int), T:Expr, E:Expr) => IfExp(V, T, E) ... </k>
    99	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   100	       [priority(40)]
   101	  rule <k> ref(H:Int) ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => V ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
   102	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   103	       [priority(40)]
   104	  // For derefs its iterable ONCE at loop start (iteration is over the snapshot;
   105	  // mutating the iterated list inside its own loop is outside the subset)
   106	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, ref(H:Int), B:Stmts) => For(T, V, B) ... </k>
   107	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   108	       [priority(40)]
   109	endmodule

--- reference-semantics/semantics/list.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST
     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule

--- reference-semantics/semantics/operators.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/operators.k — MPY-OPERATORS
     2	// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
     3	// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
     4	// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).
     5	
     6	module MPY-OPERATORS
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  imports MPY-ITER
     9	
    10	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>
    13	
    14	  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
    15	  context Compare(HOLE, _)
    16	  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
    17	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]
    18	
    19	  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
    20	  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)
    21	
    22	  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
    23	  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
    24	  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
    25	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
    26	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    27	       [priority(40)]
    28	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, ref(H:Int)) => BinOp(OP, L, V) ... </k>
    29	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    30	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // the left operand of `in`/`not in` is an ELEMENT (compares by ==K) — never deref'd
    34	  rule <k> Compare(ref(H:Int), CmpOp(OP:String, R:Expr)) => Compare(V, CmpOp(OP, R)) ... </k>
    35	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    36	       requires OP =/=String "in" andBool OP =/=String "not in"
    37	       [priority(40)]
    38	  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
    39	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    40	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    41	        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
    45	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule

--- reference-semantics/semantics/int.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/int.k — MPY-INT
     2	// Int cases of the operator dispatch; Python // and % are floored (pyMod).
     3	
     4	module MPY-INT
     5	  imports MPY-CORE
     6	
     7	  rule applyUn("-", I:Int) => 0 -Int I
     8	
     9	  rule applyBin("+",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 +Int I2
    10	  // Bool participates in int arithmetic (x += (a == b))
    11	  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, B:Bool) => I +Int #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi
    12	  rule applyBin("+",  B:Bool, I:Int) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi +Int I
    13	  rule applyBin("-",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 -Int I2
    14	  rule applyBin("*",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 *Int I2
    15	  rule applyBin("%",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => pyMod(I1, I2)
    16	  rule applyBin("//", I1:Int, I2:Int) => (I1 -Int pyMod(I1, I2)) /Int I2
    17	  rule applyBin("**", I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 ^Int I2 requires I2 >=Int 0
    18	
    19	  syntax Int ::= pyMod(Int, Int) [function]
    20	  rule pyMod(I1:Int, I2:Int) => ((I1 %Int I2) +Int I2) %Int I2
    21	
    22	  rule applyCmp("<",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <Int  I2
    23	  rule applyCmp("<=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <=Int I2
    24	  rule applyCmp(">",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >Int  I2
    25	  rule applyCmp(">=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >=Int I2
    26	  rule applyCmp("==", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 ==Int I2
    27	  rule applyCmp("!=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 =/=Int I2

// reference/src/semantics/assert.k — MPY-ASSERT

module MPY-ASSERT
  imports MPY-CORE

  rule <k> Assert(V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> Assert(V:Val) ~> _ => .K </k>
       <exc> NoExc => AssertionError </exc>
       <exit-code> _ => 1 </exit-code>
       requires notBool truthy(V)

  rule <k> Assert(ref(H:Int)) => Assert(V) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/concrete.k — MPY-CONCRETE
// Concrete-execution-only rules, visible ONLY to the llvm build (run.sh kompiles
// MPY-CONCRETE; verification builds import MPY and never see these). Rationale:
// a k-cell rule matching value constructors NARROWS abstract Vals in the haskell
// backend ([concrete] is not respected on rewrite rules) — probed on
// 26-remove-duplicates, where element compares branched into deepEqVS.

module MPY-CONCRETE
  imports MPY

  // deep equality for list compares whose elements are heap objects
  // (list-of-lists): Python == is structural at every depth.
  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("==", list(B:ValSeq))) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("!=", list(B:ValSeq))) => notBool deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)

  // ==== keyed sort, concrete leg ============================================
  // Computes each key by a REAL call through the uniform #callee machinery
  // (closures, len, type objects all work), stable-inserts on the key, and
  // allocates the result. priority(40) beats sort.k's opaque rules, so krun
  // runs this and proofs (which never see MPY-CONCRETE) keep sortKeyVS.
  syntax Val ::= kvP(Val, Val)
  syntax KItem ::= #ksort(ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
                 | #ksIns(Val, ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, false) ... </k>
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, RB) ... </k>
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #ksort(.ValSeq, _:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
        => #alloc(list(condRev(unpairVS(ACC), RB))) ... </k>
  rule <k> #ksort(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
        => KV ~> #callee((V, .Exprs)) ~> #ksIns(V, R, KV, ACC, RB) ... </k>
  rule <k> K:Val ~> #ksIns(V:Val, R:ValSeq, KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
        => #ksort(R, KV, insPair(ACC, K, V), RB) ... </k>
       requires notBool isKwV(K)

  syntax ValSeq ::= insPair(ValSeq, Val, Val) [function]
  rule insPair(.ValSeq, K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(kvP(K, V), .ValSeq)
  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    => vCons(kvP(K, V), vCons(kvP(K2, V2), R))
       requires kLt(K, K2)
  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    => vCons(kvP(K2, V2), insPair(R, K, V))
       requires notBool kLt(K, K2)

  syntax Bool ::= kLt(Val, Val) [function]
  rule kLt(I1:Int, I2:Int)             => I1 <Int I2
  rule kLt(F1:Float, F2:Float)         => F1 <Float F2
  rule kLt(str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)

  syntax ValSeq ::= unpairVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
  rule unpairVS(.ValSeq) => .ValSeq
  rule unpairVS(vCons(kvP(_:Val, V:Val), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R))
  rule unpairVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R)) [owise]
endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/bool.k — MPY-BOOL
     2	// Bool operator cases + the truthy boolean operations (not / and / or; and-or are
     3	// value-returning short-circuit over any Vals, per Python).

     5	module MPY-BOOL

     7	
     8	  rule applyUn("not", V:Val) => notBool truthy(V)

    10	  rule applyCmp("==", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 ==Bool B2
    11	  rule applyCmp("!=", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 =/=Bool B2
    12	
    13	  // ==== BoolOp: short-circuit, value-returning and / or =====================
    14	  // the node is its own accumulator: heat the HEAD element only, then either return it
    15	  // (short-circuit) or drop it and continue
    16	  context BoolOp(_, (HOLE:Expr, _:Exprs))
    17	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (V:Val, .Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    18	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    19	       requires truthy(V)
    20	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    21	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    22	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    23	       requires truthy(V)
    24	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    25	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    26	
    27	  // ==== heap-object head: decide truthiness THROUGH the heap, never rewrite the
    28	  // operand — and/or return the OBJECT itself (Python identity), not its structure
    29	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (ref(H:Int), .Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       requires truthy(V)
    34	       [priority(40)]
    35	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    36	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    37	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    38	       [priority(40)]
    39	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       requires truthy(V)
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    46	       [priority(40)]

     1	// reference/src/semantics/concrete.k — MPY-CONCRETE
     2	// Concrete-execution-only rules, visible ONLY to the llvm build (run.sh kompiles
     3	// MPY-CONCRETE; verification builds import MPY and never see these). Rationale:
     4	// a k-cell rule matching value constructors NARROWS abstract Vals in the haskell
     5	// backend ([concrete] is not respected on rewrite rules) — probed on
     6	// 26-remove-duplicates, where element compares branched into deepEqVS.
     7	
     8	module MPY-CONCRETE
     9	  imports MPY
    10	
    11	  // deep equality for list compares whose elements are heap objects
    12	  // (list-of-lists): Python == is structural at every depth.
    13	  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("==", list(B:ValSeq))) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
    14	       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
    15	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    16	  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("!=", list(B:ValSeq))) => notBool deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
    17	       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
    18	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    19	
    20	  // ==== keyed sort, concrete leg ============================================
    21	  // Computes each key by a REAL call through the uniform #callee machinery
    22	  // (closures, len, type objects all work), stable-inserts on the key, and
    23	  // allocates the result. priority(40) beats sort.k's opaque rules, so krun
    24	  // runs this and proofs (which never see MPY-CONCRETE) keep sortKeyVS.
    25	  syntax Val ::= kvP(Val, Val)
    26	  syntax KItem ::= #ksort(ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    27	                 | #ksIns(Val, ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
    29	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, false) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    32	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, RB) ... </k>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	  rule <k> #ksort(.ValSeq, _:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    35	        => #alloc(list(condRev(unpairVS(ACC), RB))) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #ksort(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    37	        => KV ~> #callee((V, .Exprs)) ~> #ksIns(V, R, KV, ACC, RB) ... </k>
    38	  rule <k> K:Val ~> #ksIns(V:Val, R:ValSeq, KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    39	        => #ksort(R, KV, insPair(ACC, K, V), RB) ... </k>
    40	       requires notBool isKwV(K)
    41	
    42	  syntax ValSeq ::= insPair(ValSeq, Val, Val) [function]
    43	  rule insPair(.ValSeq, K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(kvP(K, V), .ValSeq)
    44	  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    45	    => vCons(kvP(K, V), vCons(kvP(K2, V2), R))
    46	       requires kLt(K, K2)
    47	  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    48	    => vCons(kvP(K2, V2), insPair(R, K, V))
    49	       requires notBool kLt(K, K2)
    50	
    51	  syntax Bool ::= kLt(Val, Val) [function]
    52	  rule kLt(I1:Int, I2:Int)             => I1 <Int I2
    53	  rule kLt(F1:Float, F2:Float)         => F1 <Float F2
    54	  rule kLt(str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    55	
    56	  syntax ValSeq ::= unpairVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    57	  rule unpairVS(.ValSeq) => .ValSeq
    58	  rule unpairVS(vCons(kvP(_:Val, V:Val), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R))
    59	  rule unpairVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R)) [owise]
    60	endmodule

--- reference-semantics/semantics/dict.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/dict.k — MPY-DICT
     2	//
     3	// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
     4	// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
     5	// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
     6	// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
     7	// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
     8	//
     9	// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
    10	// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
    11	// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.
    12	
    13	module MPY-DICT
    14	  imports MPY-CORE
    15	  imports MPY-ITER
    16	  imports MPY-METHODS
    17	  imports MPY-LIST
    18	
    19	  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).
    20	  syntax Val ::= dictV(ValSeq, ValSeq)
    21	
    22	  // ==== DictExpr: {k: v, ...} literal. Eval each key then value, left to right, insert-with-dedup.
    23	  syntax KItem ::= #dictAcc(Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    24	                 | #dictKey(Expr, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    25	                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    26	  rule <k> DictExpr(ES:Entries) => #dictAcc(ES, .ValSeq, .ValSeq) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #dictAcc(.Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq) => dictV(KS, VS) ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    29	        => K ~> #dictKey(V, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    31	        => V ~> #dictVal(KV, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    32	  rule <k> VV:Val ~> #dictVal(KV:Val, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    33	        => #dictAcc(REST, dPutK(KS, KV), dPutV(KS, VS, KV, VV)) ... </k>
    34	
    35	  // insert-with-dedup helpers (concrete Val key equality via ==K). [total] so buildFold over a dict is
    36	  // total (its #Ceil is #Top) — needed when a symbolic proof carries a built dict as a config value.
    37	  syntax Bool ::= dHasKey(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    38	  rule dHasKey(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => false
    39	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => true          requires A ==K K
    40	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), K:Val) => dHasKey(R, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
    41	
    42	  // dPutK: KS unchanged if K already present, else append K (keep-first-position).
    43	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutK(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    44	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => KS                                  requires dHasKey(KS, K)
    45	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => valSeqConcat(KS, vCons(K, .ValSeq)) requires notBool dHasKey(KS, K)
    46	
    47	  // dPutV: parallel to KS — set the value at K's position if present, else append V at the end. The
    48	  // [owise] catch-all covers the degenerate mismatched-length case (never reached for a well-formed dict).
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutV(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val, Val) [function, total]
    50	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)  => vCons(V, VR)
    51	       requires A ==K K
    52	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(B, dPutV(KR, VR, K, V))
    53	       requires notBool (A ==K K)
    54	  rule dPutV(_KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq, _K:Val, V:Val) => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq)) [owise]
    55	
    56	  // ==== dict methods ========================================================
    57	  // d.keys() -> a FRESH list object of the ordered keys (k-cell: it allocates).
    58	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(dictV(KS:ValSeq, _:ValSeq), "keys")), .Vals)
    59	        => #alloc(list(KS)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	
    62	  // ==== dict subscript READ: d[k] (assoc lookup; KeyError is out of subset) ==
    63	  rule applyIndexD(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KS, VS, K)
    64	  syntax Val ::= applyIndexD(Val, Val) [function]
    65	  rule <k> Subscript(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => applyIndexD(dictV(KS, VS), K) ... </k>
    66	       [priority(45)]
    67	
    68	  // ==== dict subscript-assign: d[k] = v (insert/update in place) =============
    69	  // Only for a LOCAL dict variable X (the current scope holds it). Reuses dPutK/dPutV.
    70	  syntax Val ::= dictSet(Val, Val, Val) [function]
    71	  rule dictSet(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => dictV(dPutK(KS, K), dPutV(KS, VS, K, V))
    72	
    73	  // RHS evaluates first (Assign strictness), then the key. Dispatch on the scope
    74	  // value: a bare dict updates in the scope (dicts stay values); a ref (a heap
    75	  // list — or a heap dict later) writes the heap in place.
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetK(String, Val)
    77	  rule <k> Assign(Subscript(Name(X:String), K:Expr), VV:Val) => K ~> #dsetK(X, VV) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    79	       <env> L:Int </env>
    80	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- dictSet({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ], _) ... </scopes>
    81	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    82	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => #dsetV({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ... </k>
    83	       <env> L:Int </env>
    84	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    85	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetV(Val, Val, Val)
    87	  rule <k> #dsetV(ref(H:Int), I:Int, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
    89	  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
    90	  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    92	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    93	
    94	  // ==== dict == (order-insensitive: same size + same key->value pairs) =======
    95	  rule applyCmp("==", dictV(KS1:ValSeq, VS1:ValSeq), dictV(KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq))
    96	    => (vsLen(KS1) ==Int vsLen(KS2)) andBool dSubset(KS1, VS1, KS2, VS2)
    97	  syntax Bool ::= dSubset(ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    98	  rule dSubset(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:ValSeq, _:ValSeq) => true
    99	  rule dSubset(vCons(K:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(V:Val, VR:ValSeq), KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq)
   100	    => dHasKey(KS2, K) andBool (dGet(KS2, VS2, K) ==K V) andBool dSubset(KR, VR, KS2, VS2)
   101	  syntax Val ::= dGet(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val) [function]
   102	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => B                requires A ==K K
   103	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KR, VR, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
   104	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/sort.k — MPY-SORT
     2	// Trusted sorted(): sorted(list) as an opaque ascending permutation `sortVS` — opaque symbolic
     3	// for kprove (a trusted primitive, correctness/ordering proved in Lean / notes/sort-probe),
     4	// and a concrete insertion sort for krun. Wrappers verify the logic AROUND the sort (index /
     5	// slice / filter / dedup); indexing an opaque sortVS(VS) carries through as an opaque term, so
     6	// no ordering lemma is needed in K — the trust (sortVS = real sorted) is discharged by each
     7	// problem's differential test. Only int lists (compared by projectIntTotal); keyed / string
     8	// sorts are separate. Fires only via the "sorted" builtin, so inert for non-sorting programs.
     9	
    10	module MPY-SORT
    11	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    12	  imports MPY-SUBSCRIPT
    13	
    14	  // sortVS(VS): the ascending sort of the Val list VS. Opaque for symbolic VS (no-evaluators);
    15	  // concrete insertion sort for krun.
    16	  // Concrete sort matches Int-sorted elements directly (an int Val IS an Int); projectIntTotal
    17	  // (lemmas-only) is not available in the semantics. Int and str lists.
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortVS(ValSeq) [function, total, symbol(sortVS), no-evaluators]
    19	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVS(Int, ValSeq) [function]
    20	  rule sortVS(.ValSeq)                => .ValSeq          [concrete]
    21	  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Int, R:ValSeq)) => insVS(X, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    22	  rule insVS(X:Int, .ValSeq)                => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
    23	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R)) requires X <=Int Y [concrete]
    24	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVS(X, R)) requires X  >Int Y [concrete]
    25	  // str elements insert by the shared lexicographic strLt (methods.k)
    26	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVSs(IntSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    27	  rule sortVS(vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => insVSs(CS, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    28	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => vCons(str(A), .ValSeq) [concrete]
    29	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(A), vCons(str(B), R))
    30	       requires strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B [concrete]
    31	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(B), insVSs(A, R))
    32	       requires notBool (strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B) [concrete]
    33	
    34	  // sorted(list) constructs a NEW object: k-cell pre-dispatch (beats the [owise]
    35	  // applyBuiltin routing in call.k) so the result allocates.
    36	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
    37	        => #alloc(list(sortVS(VS))) ... </k>
    38	
    39	  // mutator: xs.sort() — the in-place heap write over the same trusted sortVS
    40	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "sort")), .Vals) => noneV ... </k>
    41	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => sortVS(VS)) ... </heap>
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  // ==== keyed / reversed sorted() (WP2) =====================================
    45	  // sortKeyVS(VS, KV): the stable ascending sort of VS by the key value KV
    46	  // (a closure/builtin/type — anything callable). OPAQUE here; the concrete
    47	  // leg (MPY-CONCRETE, llvm only) computes keys by REAL calls and stable-
    48	  // inserts, at priority(40) over these.
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortKeyVS(ValSeq, Val) [function, total, symbol(sortKeyVS), no-evaluators]
    50	
    51	  syntax ValSeq ::= revVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    52	                  | revVSAcc(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    53	  rule revVS(S:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(S, .ValSeq)
    54	  rule revVSAcc(.ValSeq, A:ValSeq) => A
    55	  rule revVSAcc(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), A:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(R, vCons(V, A))
    56	
    57	  syntax ValSeq ::= condRev(ValSeq, Bool) [function, total]
    58	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, false) => S
    59	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, true)  => revVS(S)
    60	
    61	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
    62	        => #alloc(list(sortKeyVS(VS, KV))) ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    64	        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortKeyVS(VS, KV), RB))) ... </k>
    65	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    66	        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortVS(VS), RB))) ... </k>
    67	
    68	  // Indexing the opaque sorted list: `valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), I)` is DEFINED because valSeqAt is
    69	  // [total] (subscript.k) — it stays an abstract total value for a symbolic sort and reduces
    70	  // over the concrete sort for krun. No separate sortedAt indirection is needed; wrappers write
    71	  // their postcondition directly as valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), …).
    72	endmodule

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a source-ordered exhaustive declaration/rule inventory."""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import re
from pathlib import Path


WORK = Path("/tmp/audit-work/68-pluck")
OUTPUT = Path("/audit-output/evidence/k-rule-inventory.md")
SOURCE_FILES = [
    WORK / "reference-semantics" / "semantics.k",
    *sorted((WORK / "reference-semantics" / "semantics").glob("*.k")),
    WORK / "verification.k",
    WORK / "spec.k",
]
START = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(requires|module|imports|syntax|configuration|context|rule|claim|priority|endmodule)\b"
)


def declarations(path: Path):
    lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
    starts: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        match = START.match(line)
        if match:
            starts.append((index, match.group(1)))
    for position, (start, kind) in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[position + 1][0] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        block = lines[start:end]
        while block and (not block[-1].strip() or block[-1].lstrip().startswith("//")):
            block.pop()
        yield start + 1, start + len(block), kind, "\n".join(block)


def tags(kind: str, block: str) -> list[str]:
    result: list[str] = []
    if kind == "syntax":
        for tag in (
            "function",
            "functional",
            "total",
            "symbol",
            "no-evaluators",
            "macro-rec",
            "macro",
            "token",
            "strict",
            "seqstrict",
        ):
            if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(tag)}\b", block):
                result.append(tag)
        if "no-evaluators" in block:
            result.append("opaque")
    elif kind == "rule":
        result.append("operational" if "<k>" in block else "pure/equational")
        if "simplification" in block:
            result.append("simplification")
        else:
            result.append("ordinary")
        for tag in (
            "priority",
            "owise",
            "concrete",
            "symbolic",
            "preserves-definedness",
            "macro-rec",
            "macro",
            "anywhere",
        ):
            if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(tag)}\b", block):
                result.append(tag)
    elif kind == "claim":
        result.append("reachability-claim")
    return result

    totals: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    per_file: dict[str, collections.Counter[str]] = {}
    rendered: list[str] = []
    for path in SOURCE_FILES:
        relative = path.relative_to(WORK).as_posix()

    if not root.is_dir() or root.is_symlink():
        raise KleanExportError(f"tree root must be a real directory: {root}")
    entries: list[tuple[str, str, Path]] = []
    pending = [root]
    while pending:
        directory = pending.pop()
        for child in os.scandir(directory):
            path = Path(child.path)
            mode = child.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_mode
            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
            if stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
                entries.append((relative, "directory", path))
                pending.append(path)
            elif stat.S_ISREG(mode):
                entries.append((relative, "file", path))
            else:
                raise KleanExportError(
                    f"tree contains linked or unsupported entry: {path}"

    return sorted(entries)


def tree_digest(root: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for relative, kind, path in _tree_entries(Path(root)):
        digest.update(relative.encode() + b"\0" + kind.encode() + b"\0")
        if kind == "file":
            digest.update(path.read_bytes())

`[1,3]`, `[4,2,3]`, and `[2,2]`. I substituted these values into the claimed
recursive result. All five ground summary claims printed `#Top` and exited 0:

```text
[]        -> []
[0]       -> [0,0]
[1,3]     -> []
[4,2,3]   -> [2,1]
[2,2]     -> [2,0]
```

These values also match both Python implementations in the independent
differential run. Evidence: `spec-ground-summaries.k` in scratch and
`evidence/13-ground-summary-proof.log`.

The result is not free or implied only one way: the returned reference and
exact heap payload are constrained functions of `INPUT`. The recursive
definitions embody the minimum-even/first-index property: strict replacement
selects the first even and only a later strictly smaller even; structural
induction over the finite sequence gives the stated contract.

## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review

The source-ordered exhaustive inventory is
`evidence/k-rule-inventory.md`; its generator and command record are
`evidence/k_inventory.py` and `evidence/08-inventory.log`. It enumerates all 26
K source files, 237 syntax declarations, 717 rules (238 operational and 479
pure/equational), 45 priority rules, 155 function-syntax declarations, 117
`total` declarations, 23 opaque/no-evaluator declarations, six proof-local
simplification rules, and both claims. There are no `functional`
declarations.

The detailed constructor map, per-file disposition, proof-local rule table,
evaluation-order analysis, state footprint, overlap analysis, and claim review
are in `evidence/static-review-matrix.md`.

The material findings are:

- The submitted term uses only module/function loading, plain closure calls,
  local assignment, integer operations/comparisons, list iteration, `If`,
  `Return`, and list allocation. Fixed rules preserve left-to-right evaluation,
  scope/stack lifecycle, allocation, exceptions, and abrupt return.
- None of the 23 fixed opaque symbols (float, sort, MD5, and related
  primitives) is reachable from this integer/list program. `MPY-CONCRETE` is
  not imported into the proof module.
- All fixed priority alternatives are either the faithful special case or
  pattern/guard-disjoint from the reachable plain integer/list state. There is
  no proof-local priority or operational rule.
- `verification.k` contains 22 pure equations and ten syntax declarations.
  `allNonNegative`, `shouldTake`, `nextBest`, `nextBestIndex`, `scanBest`,
  `scanBestIndex`, `afterIndex`, and `resultList` have exhaustive constructors
  or complementary/disjoint guards and structurally decreasing recursion.
- `projectIntTotal` is opaque only outside the integer sort. Every target use is
  guarded by `isInt` through `allNonNegative`/the loop precondition. Its
  guarded cast laws fix its accepted-domain value.
- The guarded `applyBin("+", Val, Int)` simplifier is a pure derived lemma, not
  a `<k>` operational bridge. On its complete guard, `Val` denotes an `Int`,
  and its RHS agrees with the fixed typed integer-addition rule.

I compiled a separate proof definition that omitted the candidate's
`applyBin` simplifier. In it, universal typed and explicit guarded-cast
connection claims, the projection identity, and a ground projection claim all
printed `#Top` and exited 0
(`evidence/17-kompile-projection-base.log`,
`evidence/19-projection-typed-connection-proof.log`). A first diagnostic
formulation left the downcast implicit and stayed stuck because fixed K could
not refine a dynamic `Val` solely from `isInt`; that narrower evidence gap is
preserved in `evidence/18-projection-connection-proof.log` and is discharged
by the explicit casted theorem. It is not a false-rule witness.

Opposite ground interpretations `projectIntTotal(7) = 8` and
`applyBin("+",7,0) = 8` both built and were rejected with the actual residual
value 7 (`evidence/20-projection-wrong-dry-run.log`,
`evidence/21-projection-wrong-proof.log`,
`evidence/25-wrong-addition-proof.log`).

No inventoried proof-local rule admits a false conclusion on the intended
domain. In particular there is no answer-encoding operational rewrite,
unconstrained result oracle, call/loop/return bypass, fabricated state, or
exception/control mismatch.

## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test

I did not rely on the candidate's `spec-vacuity.k`. The fresh reviewer mutation
`/tmp/audit-work/68-pluck/spec-audit-false-value.k` executes the exact real
body on satisfying input `[4,2,3]` but changes the result value obligation from
the true `[2,1]` to the false `[4,1]`.

Its dry run:

```text
kprove spec-audit-false-value.k \
  --definition audit-verification-kompiled \
  --spec-module SPEC-AUDIT-FALSE-VALUE --dry-run
```

exited 0, establishing successful parsing/build
(`evidence/23-fresh-false-value-dry-run.log`). The real proof command exited 1
with `WarnStuckClaimState`. Its residual was a normally completed call with
heap `0 |-> list(vCons(2,vCons(1,.ValSeq)))`, exactly the true `[2,1]`, which
could not unify with mutated `[4,1]`
(`evidence/24-fresh-false-value-proof.log`). This is the expected unmet
result obligation, not a parser error, crash, timeout, or unreachable mutation.

As separate body-sensitivity evidence, I reran the inspected opposite-comparison
body under the fresh definition. It exited 1 with a normally completed residual
heap `[4,0]`, not the original `[2,1]`
(`evidence/22-candidate-body-mutation-clean.log`). The changed constructor was
inside the closure actually executed by that claim.

## 7. Proven versus assumed accounting

The successful reachability proof establishes:

> For every finite algebraic list whose elements are non-negative K integers,
> if the exact submitted `pluck` call terminates under the supplied MPY
> semantics from the stated standard initial state, it completes normally and
> returns `[]` iff no even value is present; otherwise it returns the smallest
> even value and the least index at which that value occurs.

The theorem is unbounded in symbolic list length. It therefore covers the
prompt's empty case and all lengths through 10,000 (and proves the same property
for larger finite lists). It does not materially narrow the HumanEval domain.

Trust/assumption ledger:

- **Supplied MPY semantics and K builtin theories.** Trusted at the benchmark's
  supplied-semantics boundary, after exact tree-integrity verification. The
  rule review additionally checked every material path and established that
  unused opaque primitives cannot influence this theorem.
- **K 7.1.293 compiler, Haskell prover, LLVM executor, and reachability-logic
  implementation.** Ordinary machine-checking trust. All definitions used for
  audit results were freshly built.
- **Trusted `py2mpy.py` as the Python-to-MPY bridge.** The submitted MPY is its
  byte-identical output. Translator correctness for these AST constructors is
  an external front-end assumption, supported by direct source inspection,
  parsed-term pinning, concrete MPY execution, and Python differential tests.
- **Guarded K sort projection laws.** These affect the result but are fixed on
  every accepted input by `isInt`, the partial downcast, the static-Int
  collapse, and the bridge-free typed/casted connection proof. The opaque
  non-integer interpretation is outside the entry precondition.
- **Summary-to-English reading.** The scan equations themselves are the formal
  postcondition; the minimum-even/first-index interpretation follows by the
  stated elementary structural induction. Differential testing supplies broad
  finite corroboration only.
- **Partial correctness.** No separate liveness, time-complexity, or
  termination theorem is claimed. Negative/non-integer nodes, Python `bool`
  values as nodes, arbitrary ambient heaps/aliases, and behavior outside the
  supplied MPY subset are excluded.

Gate A (real-program soundness), Gate B (intent adequacy), and Gate C
(auditability/trust evidence) all pass. The fresh proof is result-constraining,
pins the real generated body, covers the full material source-contract domain,
and has no material semantic or proof-rule soundness gap.
